- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.03 to +0.37 in sentiment) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.40 to -0.50) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lagged corrections: if sentiment turns negative mid-period, model often doesn’t adjust forecast downward until later days.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, especially in 30-day horizon — prices often revert to 70–73 range after spikes.
- Overshoot after positive sentiment spikes — model assumes momentum continues, but sentiment decay or reversal triggers correction.
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., -0.37 to -0.50 over 3–5 days), reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid overconfidence in rebound.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment decay often outpaces model’s lagged response.
